reason: E1 directly supports HfO2 scale formation, reduced weight gain, and Zr diffusion into the Hf coating on a refractory HEA, but the substrate is not zirconium alloy and the coating is 120 µm, not 'thin'. E2 concerns AlNbTiZr coatings on Zr alloy for corrosion resistance, not Hf coatings or high-temperature oxidation, so it does not support the key premises. The cited evidence thus provides partial support for some premises but leaves others (adhesion, application method on Zr alloy) unsupported or misrepresented.
premises: Hf-rich coating forms a dense, protective HfO2 scale during high-temperature oxidation
HfO2 scale reduces oxidation weight gain compared to uncoated material
Zr diffuses into the Hf coating to form a graded interfacial layer
The graded Hf–Zr layer enhances coating adhesion and mechanical integrity
The coating can be applied by RF magnetron sputtering or hot-press sintering
